summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: ENGLISH WAYS AND BY-WAYS (Parks, Leighton; Gutenberg 76393; 1920)

**Frame:** Letters from John and Ruth Dobson, a young American clergyman couple, written from England to friend Leighton Parks (who is temporarily blind, reads via Miss Fuller; Parks was at Rectory/California). Narrator alternates: John (ch. I-II, IV-V?, XVII-XVIII area), Ruth writes some (IX, XII-XIII, XIV-XV partly), each chapter a letter. Dedicated to E.S.P. Preface: purpose is humorous record of two American impressions of pre-war England, "the test of friendship is sympathetic banter." Thanks Atlantic Monthly. Point-au-Pic, Quebec, Aug 1920.

**Chapters (titles):** I The Legacy; II School of Instruction; III "Fool Proof"; IV "Der Kaiser Wilhelm der Zweite"; V Car Arrives; VI Great North Road; VII England of Fielding; VIII End of North Road; IX English Interior; X Husband and Wife; XI Fourth Speed; XII "Jael the Wife of Heber the Kenite"; XIII "As It Was in the Beginning"; XIV Rural England; XV Education; XVI By-Election; XVII Sheep-Dogs; XVIII Brigands and Bootblacks; XIX Piston-Rod; XX Falstaff; XXI Black Country; XXII "Average" Sunday; XXIII Dowager and Cowboy; XXIV "By Pureness..."; XXV County Families; XXVI Boat-Race; XXVII Custom-House; XXVIII "Rob" Room; XXIX Vested Interests; XXX "The Auld Un'"; XXXI Church and State; XXXII Chaplain to the Queen; XXXIII Retired Colonel; XXXIV Problem in Casuistry; XXXV Day of Trouble and Distress; XXXVI "One Every Minute"; XXXVII Anglia or Frontenac?

**Key events in order:**
- I: Rex, Irish setter (gift from Mr. Dennis), dies Good Friday after John, calling "Hello, Rex!", makes it jump from study window two flights; buried at Mabel Wheelock's Pelham place; taxi $7; new Easter hat, store woman (lets Ruth keep it). Dr. Webster: "as sound as a dollar... exhausted nervous energy." Aunt Susan Melchor (California) dies, leaves money via Weeks & Burke; she was shocked by John's father's engagement to mother. John: "Well, I'll be jiggered!" "Lakewood be blowed!" -> Europe. Ruth: "lay down for a sunny day."
- II: Motor trip; Ruth's economy argument. School of Instruction under "Professor" Patrick Quinn on Jerome Avenue, NY; John drives, nearly plunges off Concourse bridge; Quinn's "O my G--d" prayer; swap. Quinn's comment on driving in Vanderbilt Cup race. John quits school.
- III: Two-cylinder demo car stalls with Ruth. Buys Frontenac runabout; salesman: "FOOL PROOF," self-starter. Practises around park three times, ships.
- IV: Crossing on the Kaiser Wilhelm der Zweite; poker invitation ("De trouble mit men..."); Sunday service in Lounge, "Ein Feste Burg"; Jewish cultivated man: "If Christians began by treating us..."; prays for Kaiser; Plymouth harbor mines fired ("childish"); Spectator, "Der Tag."
- V: Car arrives Tilbury on Georgic; third officer on docks, Venice and East River, vacuum cleaners; casual laborer "Shall I wind her up, Guv'ner?" self-starter; chauffeur on American vs English cars. Ruth to sister in Yorkshire.
- VI: Hatfield, "Purple Cow" inn; ostler, "Ichabod"; Hatfield House; Godkin, Salisbury, Allen; wrong road, twenty miles too far east, Royston; Jeanie Deans, Squeers, Pickwick.
- VII: "Dappled Hart" inn at Royston(?); bar, village doctor and drummer, "convenience" debate; Fielding; Squire Westons, Dogberry; "midden."
- VIII: Head-on near-collision, driver "Henry" and wife in tonneau: "Drunk?"; John on wrong side, Mrs. Raddles; Peterborough, cathedral; mudguard crumpled in archway; Newark, Trent, Hotspur; Doncaster; Fountain's Abbey; reach the "Beeches."
- IX: The Beeches (Sir Thomas and Maud Simpson's house; Maud's sister is Ruth's sister). Servant system; Maud/Thomas dialogue; under-housemaid's "correct insolence"; Katie Hogan of Boston.
- X: Nanny Miles; Ruth's "whys"; Maud on Englishwomen and husbands; dinner announcement; Thomas explains flintlock/church custom.
- XI: Fourth speed; John's brother-in-law ("tired of life or of my wife"); Sawley hill descent, pulls fourth-speed lever not emergency brake; picnic pony cart; boy "Oh, I say!"; Ripon, Sawley; young couple "tip": switch off, let engine brake.
- XII: Sunday at cathedral; preacher on Jael as type of Virgin; John leaves; "Sands o' Dee"; evensong, "I know where thou dwellest"; "Love Divine" anthem.
- XIII: Garden man on Anglicanism, "As it was in the beginning"; Ruth's closing reflections.
- XIV: Road from "Barchester"; James the Huntsman; seal-brown horse, Derby; sheep; Ruth: "you are exactly like Crugan"; Tom Crugan's Hoboken story ("Why the hell can't you keep your belly out of my brake?").
- XV: Gloucester, Wells, Bath, Winchester; St. Cross pilgrims; Chambered Nautilus; master on Latin/public schools; Prof. Corson.
- XVI: Salisbury; Divises by-election; Labor member Bowles; vicar with blue-ribboned pony; "The King and the Church"; young man and mother.
- XVII: Wye valley; Ross; Tintern Abbey; radiator punctured by farmer's cart shaft; sheep-dog trial.
- XVIII: Captain Burchell (retired naval), wife fears brigands; Mrs. Freeman Allen joke; "boot-blacks"; Ruth laughs.
- XIX: Shropshire, Ruth's rhapsody; broken piston-rod diagnosis; flat tire, nail; "Your tire's flat!" urchin.
- XX: Shrewsbury; car skids on wet tram rails; Raven garage; Falstaff/Hotspur musings; Mr. Rhodes (historian).
- XXI: Archdeacon Williams (Saltbridge, black country); Rose, Dick; Sunday school treat; Lancashire cotton famine man; "Not living!"; "fly" = buggy; Tod Lane, Mr. Small.
- XXII: Mission chapel sermon, Parable of Sower; archdeacon on parochial schools; "Securalists."
- XXIII: John visits Williams; Ruth with Gertrude Shelburne at Deepford; Admiral Sir George Shelburne; Guy (naval officer, photo); Lady Agatha Bumstead; Cheyenne cowboy spits.
- XXIV: Ruth to Sanfords; Ipswich Pickwick inn; Ceylon tea; Mr. Sanford's non-juror bed; church; rector's cow distraint; "white one is saft"; servants' prayers.
- XXV: Leaving Sharrow; London East End; Garvin's Private Hotel; lost telegram in porters' rack; old squire and hat/Matilda; bathroom talk.
- XXVI: Boat-race (Cambridge beats Harvard, Mortlake); punt boy; Siegels at Maidenhead.
- XXVII: Jim Siegel's Frankfort trunks story; Wilson; Charlie; Maria; locksmith; Ruth on hardness.
- XXVIII: Windsor, "Purple Sow"/White Heifer; Athanasian Creed; "Rob" Room; Lady Groves (near Reading); Miss Buckthorne; "experimenting" butler story.
- XXIX: Sir William (Groves) on C of E parish; Mr. Buckthorne on parson (partridges sitting).
- XXX: Rabbit shoot; auld un' ferret killed; pheasant shot out of season; Jenkins keeper, Jock.
- XXXI: Malvern; Sunday; curate's sermon; notices with prayers for French judges (Dreyfus); smoking room; lynching talk.
- XXXII: Chester, Betws-y-Coed, porter John's voice; Rev. Henry Waitland; Queen's chaplain story (Ponsonby).
- XXXIII: Llandudno sands; children; Ruth's blue eyes; retired colonel; "My G--d!"; Dr. Weir Mitchell mosquito story.
- XXXIV: Cork; Killarney; "shirt" (slicker); Ruth "have you got your shirt on?"; cart driver "not properly got two sides"; policeman; giant liar at Blarney; Chesterfield coal-mine joke.
- XXXV: Self-starter failing; dog; level crossing, Dublin express; Ross; Ruth cries; motor shipped to Dublin; Hodges (Professor, Anne) at Shelburne; batteries charged; Dublin Castle.
- XXXVI: Frontenac Co. London; battery; Chevallier at music hall; headlights left on three weeks; "One Every Minute."
- XXXVII: Ruth pregnant (Maud sent her to doctor; "He looked like papa"); return on Adriatic; car on dock at Tilbury; baby to be named John (or Anglia/Frontenac joke).

**Recurring characters:** Ruth (wife, Boston, Norfolk/Devon stock), John (narrator, Ulster/Welsh descent, pipe, impulsive), Maud (Ruth's sister), Sir Thomas Simpson/Thomas (Maud's husband, MP), Miles (Nanny), Dr. Webster, Mabel Wheelock, Sir William/Lady Groves, Archdeacon Williams, Mr. Sanford, Admiral Shelburne, Gertrude, Lady Agatha, Siegel (Jim, Maria, Pittsburgh), Crugan.

---

## BOOK 2: 'GAINST THE MIGHT OF SPAIN (Westerman, Percy F.; Gutenberg 78984; Pilgrim Press, London)

**Narrator:** Ralph Roy, b. 6 July 1568, Crofton, Hampshire (county "Southampton"). Father Richard Roy, Queen's pilot (Titchfield Haven); mother (Mistress Roy). Father's past: Spanish Main venture with Don Iago d'Alvarez and José da Silva; silver mine of San Luis in New Spain; treachery at Rio del Foy; father drove mules over ravine, fled; married 1566. Father vanishes night of storm; "Speedie" of Brixham (really galeas of Cadiz); Ralph ~12 then, moved to Portsmouth; apprenticed.

**Ch. I-II:** Jack Staynton (son of Roger Staynton, master-gunner, Portsmouth; 2 years older, shorter, broad). Damsel of Lyme (pinnace, 21 tons, seized for piracy; Vice-Admiral Horsey). Sir Henry Radclyffe (Governor); Mayor John Highfield; Owen Tottye; Giles Bickley (Star inn). Roger Staynton's gun-chaining of Mayor (ch II). Captain Hannibal Cleat arrives; auction of Damsel (inventory dated 29 June 1582, Mayor Highfield); Cleat buys for £34.

**Ch III-V:** Ralph bound apprentice to Cleat, 6 years, premium £5. Jack hides in after-cabin floor trap (over powder). Cleat finds him, whips Ralph (blame), reveals piracy; crew (ex-prisoners) include James (red-faced mate), "Old Garge" (kindly). Jack put ashore in shallop at Portsmouth.

**Ch VI-VIII:** Piracy off Land's End; sloop Jane of Padstow sunk on Runnelstone; boy Dick Buzza spared. Silver fleet attacked near Cape Finisterre; Cleat wounded; attempts madness/powder; shoots at Ralph, dies. Spanish galleon San Josef (Hispaniola fleet) captures Damsel; Ralph taken.

**Ch IX-X:** Don Iago d'Alvarez (First Lieutenant, Tiente Po) offers deal (chart of mine); Ralph refuses; bilboes; storm; San Josef damaged, anchored at Vigo?; Ralph taken to house, sees father's Southampton Water chart ("Ric: Roy, his Mappe. A.D. 1552").

**Ch XI-XII:** Inquisition (prison, cell No. 19); meets father (captured on galeas; Escurial, King Philip). Torture chamber: father kills pikemen, familiars; Ralph kills scrivener; Chief Inquisitor killed.

**Ch XIII-XV:** Escape via chapel of San Thomé, priory garden, fishing boats; recover Damsel (felucca rig); Spanish fort fire; chase by galley; Nonsuch of Dartmouth (Master Roger Staynton, now captain, Jack aboard) rescues. Fowey storm delay. Plan for Spanish Main with Roger.

**Ch XVI-XVIII:** Expedition sails 1584 (Lady Day; Ralph's 16th birthday); Yucatan, Bay of Campechy; Vera Cruz 20 leagues; Indians; Huitzel volcano; mine of San Luis; Jenkins rescue at pass; silver taken; ambush by Spanish horse; Coombes (mate, Bosham) swims with 3 to recover Damsel; Ralph wounded (leg, head) at isthmus fight; Jack leads sally.

**Ch XIX-XX:** Ralph recovers; Nonsuch; Virginia; storm; galleon Sol del Esto (captain Don José da Silva) taken; father's leg amputated (ankle); Ralph commands; Cornish coast; Nonsuch reunited; Portsmouth.

**Ch XXI-XXV:** Armada 1588 (Ralph 20). Tocsin; Tom Slingsby (Sir Thomas Slingsby of Bramdean) joins; Fleming Scottish pirate; Damsel's topmast from Pride of Saltash; Ark Royal, Lord Howard of Effingham; Don Pedro Valdez surrenders (Revenge, Drake); Venetian ship; Slingsby wounded; fireship Damsel burned, sinks two galleons; Ralph knighted by Queen Elizabeth ("Sir Ralph Roy") after Lord Sussex (Radclyffe) speaks; Jack goes Pacific; Don Iago seen in galleys at Bordeaux (captured by French captain under Henry IV).

**Other:** Book 2 front matter ads for Pilgrim Press titles; transcriber notes.
